verdict.label: BUY / SELECTIVE — Week-Ahead: A Catalyst-Dense June Opens Into the Strongest Tape of the Series
verdict.rationale_short: Markets are closed (Sunday). This is a forward-looking week-ahead briefing positioning into the June 1 open. The setup is the strongest of the series — SPX at records, 30Y sub-5.0%, oil's worst month since 2020 — but June front-loads the densest catalyst slate of the cycle: ISM Manufacturing (Jun 1), the May jobs report (Jun 5), the SpaceX SPCX roadshow (Jun 8) and trade debut (Jun 12), and Warsh's first FOMC (Jun 16-17). Conviction holds at medium because the Iran signature is still pending and every one of these catalysts can independently re-test the BUY thesis. The plan: act on confirmation, not anticipation — scale XLE short on an Iran signing, arm the NVDA add on Day 2 of the 30Y confirmation, and keep the IWM short patient for the SPCX capital-drain window.

bear_case: The week-ahead risk is that June front-loads four independent ways for a nine-week win streak to break, each landing before Warsh even speaks. ISM Manufacturing (Jun 1) can print a contraction; the May jobs report (Jun 5) can run hot and hand Warsh cover to hike; the SPCX roadshow (Jun 8) begins draining ~$75B from liquid allocations; and the Warsh FOMC (Jun 16-17) is the first meeting of a historically hawkish chair widely expected to strip the easing bias with PCE still at 3.8% YoY. Layered on top is an Iran deal that markets have fully priced but Trump has not signed, with no constraint on Iran's nuclear stockpile. The tape enters this gauntlet at record highs with VIX at 15.32 — the cheapest hedging in weeks, which almost no one is using. Invalidation level: a hot May payroll print (>220K with firm wages) that pushes the 30Y back above 5.10%, or a daily SPX close below 7,460, converts the BUY framework to Step Aside; a June 17 Warsh hike forces an exit of all longs regardless of index level.
